runtime: Brepkit 4.2.2, Windows debug build, six-feature reproduction
method: Read-only registry inspection and separate .tools Rust diagnostic executables; no kernel or application source modified during diagnosis.

confirmed_failure.operation: Fuse rectangular slab with through side hole and a perpendicular cylinder disc
confirmed_failure.stage: GFA Builder curved-face splitting, before boolean face selection/assembly
confirmed_failure.face: Input-local face Id(8), disc cylindrical lateral, u-periodic with v spanning 0..25.4 mm
confirmed_failure.sections: 2 vertical line sections at x=0 plus 4 NURBS cylinder/cylinder intersection sections
confirmed_failure.error: face splitting failed: face Id(8) is cut by sections but split into nothing
confirmed_failure.fallback: operations::boolean then uses mesh co-refinement; CAD correctly rejects it and preserves previous exact solid

trace_observations: Angular traversal traces only one two-edge remnant and two duplicate three-edge loops at one intersection arch; the cylindrical wall band is absent.

The pre-trace graph contains repeated NURBS section edges and boundary circles at different unwrapped UV period copies. Period copies alone are legal; the trace does not establish one specific incorrect line.

The current curved-face splitter already has section deduplication, seam alignment, angular/DCEL rescue and periodic sliver guards. A safe fix needs analysis across those paths, not simply relaxing final validation.

tested_exact_alternatives.attempt: Rebuild tool as canonical analytic cylinder primitive

requirements: Preserve shared curve and edge provenance while removing duplicate trace edges
Build a consistent periodic UV sheet and enumerate the wall band plus intersection regions
